messages:
incident-bot: [P0] Tenant 'nightingale' high tail latency on dedicated pool na-1 — 95th latency > 600ms, error budget at risk. Seen since 02:03 UTC. Affected: dedicated tenant routing, responses queued. Runbook: <https://go/runbooks/tenant-bespoke-batching>. Paging eng-oncall.

alex (oncall): taking this — oncall handoff noted. First glance: spikes in queue depth for nightingale's bespoke queue. Can someone pull per-tenant queue metrics and current scheduler knobs?

maria (sre): pulling metrics now. queue_depth/nightingale up to 1200 requests, avg service_time increased, and there's a big tail at >10s GC for some worker processes. max_batch_tokens currently 8192 (tenant override).

sam (runtime): that max_batch_tokens is aggressive — nightingale uses long contexts and we end up coalescing huge batches that stall KV cache memory and cause slower kernels. Two immediate mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_tokens for nightingale to limit batch bloat, 2) enable queue isolation (route to a bespoke small-pool) to avoid head-of-line blocking. I can push a config change for #1 now.

june (solutions): FYI customer CS alerted that they saw failed requests and timeouts in their app. They want ETA on fix. I'll keep them in the loop.

alex (oncall): go ahead, sam. apply a conservative drop to 4096 and set shaper.window_ms=50 for that tenant. We'll monitor.

sam (runtime): running change via internal API:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/tenants/nightingale/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduler":{"max_batch_tokens":4096,"shaper":{"type":"adaptive","window_ms":50}}}'
```

ops-bot: automation: change request accepted, rollout id rl-20260315-3141, applying to schedulers in na-1 (3/3 nodes).

maria (sre): seeing immediate effect on incoming queues — queue_depth dropping from 1200 -> 350 in ~40s. 95th latency trending down (620ms -> 230ms). No error spike on retries.

june (solutions): passing update to CS: "We're applying temporary scheduler limits which should reduce tail latency — we'll confirm after stabilization." :thumbsup:

alex (oncall): good. Sam, can you also pin a temporary rate-limit at tenant level to smooth bursts while we evaluate? Something like 120 rps sustained, 400 burst?

sam (runtime): can do. Applying token-bucket override:

```json
{"ratelimit": {"sustained_rps": 120, "burst": 400}}
```

ops-bot: rate limit override queued, rollout id rl-20260315-3142.

maria (sre): after both changes, 95th stabilized ~200ms, p99 at ~420ms. CPU on pool nodes normalized. Memory pressure dropped on KV cache and GC pauses stopped. Looks like the large batch sizes were the primary driver.

alex (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for now. Still not 'resolved' — will keep monitoring 30m. Can someone create a follow-up ticket for: 1) permanent fix (dedicated micro-pool or smarter batching policy), 2) customer outreach and postmortem, 3) playbook update to include these knobs?

june (solutions): creating CS ticket and scheduling customer call in morning. I'll link this thread.

sam (runtime): filing internal bug + RFC: propose a new adaptive max_batch_tokens algorithm that considers recent per-request token distribution and KV cache pressure. Also recommend adding a safety cap for tenants with long-context usage.

maria (sre): note for postmortem: incident timeline, metrics dump, and the exact rollouts (rl-20260315-3141, rl-20260315-3142). I'll grab heap/GC traces for the 02:00-02:10 window.

alex (oncall): handing off to maria for overnight watch. I'm signing off for my shift in 15m. If things regress ping me directly.

maria (sre): taking watch. I'll keep a 5m poll on p95/p99 and queue_depth and update if any bounce.

incident-bot: incident status changed -> mitigated. Gov: oncall-team.

june (solutions): note for customer comms: temporary config changes applied (max_batch_tokens 8192 -> 4096, shaper.window_ms 200 -> 50, tenant rate-limit applied). We'll propose either dedicated pool or traffic-shaping for long-term.

alex (oncall): thanks team. I'll add a brief blameless note in the postmortem doc template. :coffee:
